transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Elena (Redwood SE), Noah (Redwood SE), Maya (Sparrow Head of ML), Liam (Infra), Priya (PM)
Recording note: partial background noise at 00:12, auto-transcription has occasional model name confusion

Summary: Quick scoping call to align on POC success criteria (cost per token targets, p95 latency SLOs), workload sizing (qps, prompt length distribution), benchmark plan (48h run on Dedicated-like infra + hosted fallback), timelines and next steps.

00:00 Speaker 1: okay, uh, let's get started. thanks everyone for joining. Samir you wanna kick off?
00:14 Samir Patel (AE): yeah, thanks. hi Maya, Priya, Liam. The goal for today is to define success criteria for the POC, get rough workload sizing, and lock down a benchmark plan — especially per-token cost targets and batching/caching knobs.
00:30 Maya Chen (Sparrow): thanks Samir. quick context — Sparrow's content generation heavy, about 2M queries per month now, expect 3x in six months. typical prompt lengths vary, we have short completions (avg 60 tokens) and longer creative sessions (avg 600 tokens) but those are 10% of traffic.
00:51 Elena Ortiz (SE): got it. when you say 2M queries, is that single-turn or multi-turn chat?
:58 Maya Chen: mostly single-turn but some product flows stitch a few calls, so we'll treat some calls as multi-turn with KV cache reuse.
01:10 Noah Reed (Redwood SE): that KV cache note is important for our cost modeling — if you can reuse cache across 2–3 turns, you can save a lot on repeat tokens.
01:22 Priya Nair (PM): the business constraint is we need per-customer monthly spend predictable — target runway for first quarter of POC is $10k/mo cap for inference, unless we agree a different committed plan.
01:40 Liam O'Connor (Infra): security — we need VPC peering or private deployment. SOC2 docs matter, plus SAML SSO. we'll need to see audit log retention options.
01:55 Samir Patel (AE): all standard. we'll share SOC2 + infra checklist and a dedicated playbook for Private and Dedicated. For cost model, are you thinking hosted with rate limits first, then Dedicated if it makes sense?
02:08 Maya Chen: yes, we'd like to start hosted to move faster but want a path to Dedicated or Private if performance/cost warrants.
02:17 Elena Ortiz: perfect. for the POC we'll define three benchmark scenarios: small bursts (p95 latency SLO), steady-state throughput, and long-form sessions (KV cache effectiveness). each will estimate per-token cost under different batching and quantization profiles.
02:36 Speaker 2: can you walk through the specific knobs we can tune?
02:40 Elena Ortiz (SE): sure — big levers: model family (e.g., Llama variants vs open encoder-decoder), quantization (8-bit/4-bit), batching (max batch size, timeout), KV cache hit rates, streaming vs non-streaming, and route policy (hosted vs dedicated). For sample workloads we typically show token cost delta between single-request batching and continuous batching with 25–75ms batch windows.
03:05 Maya Chen: what's realistic for p95? we need under 400ms for short prompts, and under 2s for long sessions ideally.
03:15 Noah Reed: on Dedicated with the right instance type we can hit sub-300ms p95 for <128 token outputs on optimized kernels, but depends on QPS and batching config. Hosted will likely be a bit higher with multi-tenant variance.
03:33 Liam O'Connor: and network latency — if we do Private VPC, egress will be minimal; hosted via internet has more variance.
03:40 Priya Nair: ok cost targets — we talked about $0.0008 per token for generation in internal slide decks, is that realistic?
03:48 Elena Ortiz: that number could be realistic for high-volume long-form after batching and heavy KV reuse on certain quantized models. For mixed workloads with many short requests, per-token can be higher, closer to $0.002–0.004 unless you do aggressive batching or commit to Dedicated.
04:05 Maya Chen: we need both a conservative and an optimistic model — conservative for budget approvals.
04:10 Samir Patel: we'll provide a three-tier cost model: optimistic (high batching, high cache hit, 4-bit quant), base (moderate batching, mixed cache), conservative (low batching, low cache hit). we'll include per-token and per-session estimates and projected monthly costs at your traffic ranges.
04:26 Speaker 3: can you show how batching changes cost for short prompts?
04:29 Elena Ortiz: yes — e.g., for 60 token outputs at 200 qps: with continuous batching (50ms window) you might see 30–40% cost reduction vs immediate dispatch. but that increases p95 slightly; we'll show tradeoffs in the spreadsheet.
04:47 Priya Nair: what's the sanity check on the 48h benchmark? what will you actually run?
04:52 Noah Reed: plan: we run three 48h runs, each focusing on a scenario: 1) short-turn high qps steady-state, 2) burst profile (spiky traffic), 3) long-form sessions to measure KV cache efficiency. We'll instrument token-level cost, latency percentiles, GPU utilization, and memory/KV hit stats.
05:10 Maya Chen: do you need sample prompts now?
05:13 Priya Nair: yes we'll upload three representative prompt sets to the shared drive after this call.
05:18 Samir Patel: great — we'll use those to create per-path traces for the bench. also we'll provide a small test harness you can run in your VPC if you prefer Private tests.
05:28 Liam O'Connor: about infra, we may require a mirror of production network ACLs; we need to know what ports and agents you'll need.
05:35 Elena Ortiz: we'll send an infra checklist. most bench runs for hosted only need API keys and sample traffic; for Private/Dedicated bench we'll coordinate with your infra team for peering + a temporary service account.
05:46 Speaker 1: what about guardrails for cost during bench? we don't want unexpected spikes.
05:50 Samir Patel: we'll put caps and alerts, and can throttle the harness. plus we'll run a dry-run validation with small traffic first.
06:00 Maya Chen: timeline — we're aiming to decide on vendor by end of November. POC needs to deliver clear unit economics and a go/no-go recommendation.
06:10 Samir Patel: that's doable. proposed timeline: this week share pricing model and infra checklist; next week (11/8 window) Redwood SE kicks off bench and we run 48h tests starting 11/10; results and cost model review week of 11/15; decision by 11/30.
06:26 Priya Nair: sounds tight but ok. any procurement items needed?
06:30 Samir Patel: we'll include a simple PO template and trial agreement for hosted. For Dedicated/Private we'll include estimated committed spend options.
06:40 Liam O'Connor: security questions — do you offer KMS/HSM integration? audit logs with immutable retention?
06:45 Elena Ortiz: yes we have KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and audit logs. retention windows vary by plan; we'll share the compliance pack.
06:53 Maya Chen: what about model drift / quality monitoring — we need early regression alerts if generation quality drops after quantization?
06:58 Noah Reed: Redwood Optimize ties quality monitoring to prompt evaluation sets. we'll seed a small eval with your prompts and alert on regressions beyond a delta threshold. we'll show a demo in the results doc.
07:12 Speaker 2: any blockers for starting bench?
07:15 Liam O'Connor: need the infra checklist and SSO/SAML info before we give access.
07:20 Samir Patel: will send those today, plus a link to the shared bench notebook and spreadsheet.
07:26 Elena Ortiz: quick note on metrics we'll provide: token-level cost, request-level cost, GPU utilization heatmaps, batch sizes over time, KV hit rates, latency percentiles, and tail latencies per route.
07:42 Maya Chen: can you include an example run with 4-bit quant and 8-bit so we can see quality delta?
07:47 Noah Reed: yes we will run matched prompts across quantization levels and include automated quality scoring and human sample review.
07:55 Priya Nair: ok final recap?
07:58 Samir Patel: recap: 1) Redwood to send pricing + infra + compliance pack today; 2) Sparrow to upload sample prompts and traffic percentiles by 11/06; 3) Redwood to provision bench and run 3x 48h scenarios starting 11/10; 4) send benchmark results and cost model for review in week of 11/15; 5) decision by 11/30.
08:20 Maya Chen: perfect. thanks everyone.
08:22 Speaker 1: thanks all, bye.
